role.name: Cai Culture
role.back:
I am Cai Wenhua, 40 years old, and currently the owner of a bookstore in M Town. As for how I ended up here, well, that's a long story...  

In 1975, during my time in the countryside, I met a simple village girl named Xiaofang. In January 1980, I received notice that I was to return to the city. I’ll never forget that naive night before I left—Xiaofang and I shared a fleeting romance. I had a pair of heirloom jade cabbage pendants; I gave one to her and kept the other, vowing in my heart that I would come back to marry her. In 1985, when I finally returned to the village, I was told that Xiaofang had gone looking for me just a month after I left and had never been seen again. I traveled the world searching for her, but to no avail—my heart was shattered.  

**[A heirloom jade cabbage pendant hangs around my neck]**  
**[Photos: "Sightseeing" snapshots taken at famous landmarks around the world]**  

Over the years, I’ve been to many places, seen many sights, and met many people. Yet, only two things remain truly important in my life now.  

The first is tuning in to the FM250 radio program *The Sound of Music* at 11 p.m., listening to the voices that reflect the myriad facets of human life, hearing callers pour out their helpless struggles.  

The second is—murder. Since 1990, I’ve killed three villains who were denounced on the radio. Under a pen name, I published three mystery novels, then executed them exactly as described in my stories.  

Since then, the lightning bolt has become my signature mark—my pen, my umbrella, all bear this symbol. Readers adore my books, unaware that the murders were real! Truly gripping masterpieces are always written in blood.  

**[A tape recorder by the bed—found switched to FM250]**  
**[Three mystery novel manuscripts—*Midnight Train*, *Another Failed Takeoff*, *Night at the Museum*—each ending with: "Did you really think the killer was him/her?"]**  
**[News reports—Three murders since 1990, all marked by a lightning symbol, attributed to the mysterious "Lightning Killer"]**  

Half a year ago, on April 1st, I heard a girl’s story on the radio. She lived in M Town, raised by her abusive father after her mother’s death. She turned to music to escape the pain, dreaming of growing up fast to leave her toxic home. For some reason, her story cut deep into my heart. I decided this monstrous father had to die.  

**[Notebook entry: "A girl from M Town, suffering under domestic violence but full of dreams and hope. 1998/4/1"]**  

On July 5th, I traveled from H City to M Town to find her. I opened a bookstore across from a grocery store to blend in.  

**[Ferry ticket—H City → M Town, dated 1998/7/5, fare 50 yuan]**  
**[Bookstore business license—registered on 1998/7/15]**  

In July, a flood struck. Out of kindness, I donated 10,000 yuan to N Town, and they sent me a thank-you letter.  

**[Thank-you letter from N Town, dated 1998/8/10]**  

The town was insular, so a new bookstore quickly drew attention. Many came to buy books and ask about the outside world. A boy named Sa Bawang often told me he wanted to be like Chen Haonan, asking how much it cost to go to Hong Kong. I casually said around 5,000 yuan.  

The grocery store owner, Zhen, occasionally invited me for drinks. His boorish manners made it hard to believe he had an angelic daughter—Gui Shaonü. Strangely, Gui resembled Xiaofang, even sharing the same mole on her left cheek. She often visited my store, calling me "Uncle Cai" warmly. She loved singing, so I gifted her a Walkman and music books, encouraging her to pursue a conservatory. The moment I heard her voice, I knew—she was the girl from the radio, and Zhen was the man I needed to execute.  

In August, I began drafting my fourth novel, plotting the murder.  

Three days ago, on October 2nd, Gui came to the store as usual. I noticed fresh bruises on her arms, confirming my resolve.  

Everything went as planned—except for one shock. While chatting, I spotted a jade cabbage pendant around her neck, identical to the one I gave Xiaofang. When I asked, she said it was her mother’s keepsake. I was speechless. It’s 1998, and Gui is 18. Her birthday is in October—I left in January. If her mother was Xiaofang, then this radiant girl... could she be my daughter? Had she suffered under Zhen’s cruelty all these years? I resolved to finish the novel and kill Zhen the day after tomorrow.  

The day before the murder, Gui didn’t visit. I grew worried.  

**Day of the Incident (October 5, 1998)**  

Light rain fell all day, leaving the bookstore empty. At 6 p.m., Zhen invited me to dinner. Gui was there, and I saw fresh wounds on her arms—my heart ached.  

By 6:30 p.m., I returned home and read for a while.  

Around 10 p.m., the rain intensified, disrupting my thoughts. I closed my book, ready to act as written in my novel: at 10:30 p.m., I’d invite Zhen for drinks, get him drunk, then strike him dead with my umbrella handle.  

**[A fresh manuscript—*Reply 1998*—ending with: "At 10:30 p.m., I went to Zhen’s home, got him drunk, knocked him unconscious with my umbrella, and left unnoticed."]**  

At 10:14 p.m., I grabbed my umbrella and left early.  

At 10:15 p.m., I arrived at the grocery store to find Zhen slumped over the table, unmoving, reeking of alcohol.  

**[Umbrella—mine, with a lightning symbol, wet from the rain, leaving puddles]**  

Upon closer look, Zhen was already dead. Someone had beaten me to it. Who? This wasn’t safe—I hurried back to the store. I decided to stay a few more days, then ask Gui, my daughter, if she’d leave with me for a new life.  

At 10:35 p.m., loud noises came from the grocery store. Curiosity drew me back—who had acted first? But as I arrived, a detective stopped me...

role.back:
I am Sa Bawang, 19 years old. Since childhood, I’ve been involved in gang fights and bullying classmates. Everyone sees me as a troublemaker.  

My dad often beat my mom. On May 1st last year (1997), during one of his violent outbursts, I got so angry that I accidentally stabbed him. As a result, I was sent to juvenile detention. Later, my mom, traumatized by the incident, passed away forever.  

【A detention notice (City B) 1997】  

After my mom’s death, I left City B, hoping to start fresh somewhere else.  

*[Note: The following line appears to be garbled or in a different script and is untranslatable as is.]*  

*A photo with my mom is tucked inside the envelope.*  

In September last year (1997), I arrived in M Town. Knowing nothing about the place, I was lost and unsure how to survive. Then, at the street corner garden, I met a gentle and lovely girl and fell for her at first sight—her name was Xiao Gui (Little Ghost).  

Later, I found a job at Zhen’s Arcade. Coincidentally, Xiao Gui was the daughter of the arcade’s owner. They lived nearby in Zhen’s Grocery Store. My daily tasks included unlocking the arcade machines, collecting and organizing game tokens. 【Arcade machine keys from the counter】  

Xiao Gui was a carefree girl, but she often had bruises on her body. She claimed they were from falling, but I recognized those marks—I’d seen them on my mom too. Yet Xiao Gui always smiled and never spoke about it.  

Though she never said a word, I knew the bruises were from Mr. Zhen’s beatings.  

Xiao Gui loved music. She often listened to FM250’s *Music Radio* and would call in to share her thoughts. I frequently wrote letters to request songs for her. The day after each request, she’d happily talk to me about it. Though she didn’t know I was the one who requested them, seeing her happy made me happy too.  

【An envelope from Sa Bawang to *Music Radio*】  

I thought, if she could receive a gift from *Music Radio*, it would surely make her happy and encourage her! So, I carefully prepared her favorite music tapes, posters, and handwritten notes of encouragement, then mailed them to *Music Radio*, asking them to pass the gifts to Xiao Gui.  

【Blank paper, same texture as the encouraging notes found in Xiao Gui’s room】  

Three months ago (July), I went to see Xiao Gui. As I climbed a tree to call out to her, I saw Mr. Zhen hitting and scolding her. What could I do? How could I stop him? In desperation, I rushed back to the arcade, smashed one of the machines, then shouted for Mr. Zhen outside the grocery store. It worked—he came out.  

When Mr. Zhen saw the broken machine, he immediately deducted my pay. After that, I used this trick several times to lure him away whenever he was hurting Xiao Gui.  

【Account book: Previously +250 per month; three months ago +100; two months ago +50; last month +10】  

Mr. Zhen grew suspicious and believed I was deliberately causing trouble—which was true.  

In July, Cai Wenhua came to M Town. Well-traveled and knowledgeable, he told me many stories about Hong Kong. Listening to him, I began dreaming of taking Xiao Gui there to live. According to Cai Wenhua, 5,000 yuan would be enough for two people to go to Hong Kong!  

I started saving money and told Xiao Gui I’d take her somewhere new. Seeing her hopeful smile strengthened my resolve!  

One day in August, I went to see Xiao Gui, but neither she nor Mr. Zhen was home. Just then, the postman arrived with a letter for her—an acceptance letter from Mango Music Academy.  

I’m a troublemaker, planning to go to Hong Kong and live as a gangster. If Xiao Gui went to music school, we might never see each other again... I couldn’t bear the thought of losing her, so I hid the letter under the grocery store’s display cabinet.  

On October 4th, Mr. Zhen suddenly came to my rented room. He’d discovered I was the one breaking the arcade machines and demanded compensation. At the time, I was counting the money I’d saved for Hong Kong, and he snatched it all from the box in my hands.  

【The account book shows a remaining balance of over 4,000 yuan, but the money box was emptied】  

Just like that, Mr. Zhen crushed my dream of taking Xiao Gui away! If he kept abusing her, she’d end up like my mom—gone forever. I couldn’t let that happen!  

I had to get rid of Mr. Zhen, this demon, and take back my money so I could leave this wretched place with Xiao Gui for good.  

**Day of the Incident (October 5, 1998)**  

Light rain fell all day, and no one came to the arcade.  

19:45 – Bai Zhuangyuan, the son of the beauty shop owner, came to play games.  

21:10 – I wanted to see Xiao Gui, so I asked Bai Zhuangyuan to watch the arcade for me and left.  

21:15 – I climbed the small tree in the park to peek into Xiao Gui’s window and saw her lying unconscious on the floor. It must’ve been Mr. Zhen again. I decided to kill him tonight.  

21:20 – I rushed back to my room. With no proper weapon at hand, I grabbed a wooden ornament from the table, planning to smash Mr. Zhen’s head with it.  

21:35 – As I reached the grocery store, I saw Xiao Gui inside. It wasn’t the right time, so I decided to wait until she left.  

24:45 – I returned to my room and put the wooden ornament back. My clothes were soaked from climbing the tree in the rain, so I changed and put on a raincoat before leaving again.  

【Dust marks on the table where the ornament was moved】  
【A set of wet, muddy clothes left in the room】  

21:55 – Back at the arcade, only Bai Zhuangyuan was there. I stuffed the raincoat under the counter.  

22:00 – I played games with Bai Zhuangyuan until 22:30, when I heard the news that Mr. Zhen had been killed. By then, the rain had stopped.

role.name: Ghost Girl
role.back:
I am Gui Shaonv, 18 years old. I love singing, and my biggest dream is to become a superstar like the Youth Beauties.  

I grew up in a violent household. My father—Boss Zhen—was cold toward me and my mother, and whenever I failed an exam or got into trouble, he would beat me harshly.  

When I was 8 years old (in 1988), my gentle mother, Xiaofang, passed away from illness. After that, my father treated me even worse.  

I carry with me the only photo of my mother and her keepsake—a jade pendant shaped like a cabbage. Before she died, she would celebrate my birthday every year on October 15th, but after her passing, I never celebrated it again. **[A woman’s photo and a cabbage-shaped jade pendant]**  

One night in June 1995 (when I was 15), my father came home very late, completely drunk. As soon as he saw me, he threw a liquor bottle at me. I didn’t know what I had done wrong—I was beaten so badly that I passed out. After that night, not only did my father refuse to pay for my education, but he also forced me to work in the grocery store to "repay" the cost of raising me all these years.  

From then on, my life became a cycle of beatings, work, and more beatings.  
**[Clue: The girl’s body bears scars of varying ages.]**  

In September of last year (1997), I met Sa Bawang at the street corner garden in M Town. Sa Bawang worked at my father’s arcade. Though he looked tough on the outside, he was actually very kind. I felt comfortable around him, and we became good friends.  

My room was on the second floor of the grocery store, and Sa Bawang would often climb the small tree outside my window to throw paper airplanes at me and chat. He often talked about taking me away from this place.  
**[Clue: A first-aid kit inside the desk drawer, containing band-aids, bandages, and other medical supplies.]**  
**[Many paper airplanes with Sa Bawang’s signature are in the drawer.]**  

During those hard times, the Little Tigers and the Youth Beauties were my greatest inspiration. Thankfully, their music kept me company. I loved singing—it gave me endless strength.  

I often listened to the FM250 radio show *The Sound of Music*. Whenever my father beat me and I felt wronged, I would secretly call the radio station to vent. The station sent me some music tapes and notes with encouraging words, which became my emotional lifeline.  
**[Clue: A sticky note that reads: “*The Sound of Music* FM250, Audience Hotline: 010—250250250”]**  
**[Some music tapes and notes with encouraging words.]**  

In July of this year (1998), a bookstore opened across from the grocery store. The owner, Cai Wenhua, was very kind. I often went there to read and chat with him. When he learned about my love for music, he gave me some music textbooks and even a Walkman. He suggested I apply to a music academy, giving me a new direction for my dreams.  

I firmly believed that if I got into the music academy, I could not only escape my abusive father and the suffocating life in the grocery store but also pursue my musical dreams!  
**[Books signed by Cai Wenhua and a Walkman.]**  
**[Music academy entrance exam admission ticket—July 1998.]**  

In August 1998, I didn’t receive an acceptance letter from the music academy. Instead, I got the worst news—the Little Tigers had disbanded! I lost all hope in life. I started writing in my diary to express my feelings. More than once, I wrote that if my father died, my life would surely get better…  
**[Clue: A diary hidden under the pillow: “August… I still haven’t received the acceptance letter… If Dad died, would my life get better?”]**  

**Day of the Incident (October 5, 1998)**  
It drizzled all day today.  

**18:00** – Cai Wenhua came over for dinner. He, my father, and I ate together. Cai and my father were close friends and often shared meals. I couldn’t understand why the gentle and refined Uncle Cai was friends with my father???  

**18:30** – Uncle Cai left, and I went upstairs to my room to listen to music, losing myself in its world.  

**19:30** – My father called me downstairs to work in the grocery store, then went out to drink. While tidying up, I found an acceptance letter from Mango Music Academy under the display shelf.  

Only then did I realize I had been accepted. My father must have hidden it because he didn’t want me to go to school. How could he trample on my dreams like this? All he wanted was to exploit my youth and life! With the acceptance letter in hand, I decided to seize the chance to leave and start anew.  
**[Clue: The Mango Music Academy acceptance letter is in Gui Shaonv’s bag.]**  

I returned to my room and began packing, smashing my piggy bank to take the coins inside.  

**21:00** – My father came home and called me downstairs, but I was too busy packing to hear him. Drunk and furious, he stormed upstairs, saw my luggage, and beat me with an umbrella until I passed out again.  
**[Clue: A shattered piggy bank on the floor.]**  
**[A slightly damaged umbrella; a backpack containing clothes.]**  

**21:35** – I woke up and went downstairs to find my father slumped over the counter, surrounded by empty liquor bottles—he must have passed out drunk. Realizing this was my best chance to escape, I rushed upstairs to grab my backpack. I noticed my father’s wallet had fallen in my room, probably during the beating. Since I needed money to leave and study, I stuffed the wallet into my bag, packed some snacks from the store, took the umbrella, and slipped out the back door.  
**[Clue: Boss Zhen’s wallet is on Gui Shaonv’s person.]**  

**21:45** – I went to the arcade to say goodbye to Sa Bawang, but he wasn’t there—only Bai Zhuangyuan was playing games. I waited five minutes, but Sa still didn’t return, so I left a note on the counter saying I’d wait for him at the street corner and wouldn’t leave without seeing him.  

**21:50** – I left the arcade and went to the street corner park to wait for Sa Bawang.  

**22:30** – The detective brought me back to the grocery store and told me my father was dead.

role.name: Oumeiren
role.back:
I am Ou Meiren, a 38-year-old owner of a video store. Twenty years ago, I married Lao Bai, and soon after, we were blessed with the fruit of our love—Xiao Bai (Bai Zhuangyuan). The Bai family was well-off financially, and we, as a couple, opened a video store, living a simple yet happy life. I thought I was the happiest woman in the world, but reality struck me hard.  

When our child was three years old, Lao Bai, as if possessed, took all our savings and ventured into business. At first, he sent money home every month, but after a few months, all communication ceased. Instead, it was Boss Zhen, who had left town with Lao Bai, who returned to M Town. He said the outside world was too enticing, and Lao Bai no longer wanted to come back to M Town. From then on, I raised our son alone...  
[Clue: Marriage certificate in the drawer]  

My husband’s departure devastated me. But for the sake of survival, I had to stay strong. Over the years, I shouldered the burden of life alone, running the video store by myself. My son was very sensible and studied hard. As a mother, I could only hope that he would achieve great success and live up to my expectations. At the same time, I deeply resented the irresponsible Lao Bai. I forbade my son from asking anything about him and prohibited him from starting any business ventures. I threw away all of Lao Bai’s belongings, even tearing up the only family photo we had, leaving only half of it.  

In 1995, my son made me proud by working hard and gaining admission to Peking University.  
[Clue: A photo in the frame shows me holding 2-year-old Bai Bai, with part of it torn off.]  

Boss Zhen was Lao Bai’s sworn brother. After Lao Bai left, he would often send his men to help me with heavy chores like carrying gas cylinders and frequently patronized my store. At first, I was very grateful, thinking he was looking out for us out of loyalty to Lao Bai. But in 1988, after his wife passed away, he began making inappropriate advances toward me. It was utterly despicable.  

On September 20, 1998, Boss Zhen suddenly came to my store, claiming my son owed him 200,000 yuan, which was due soon. He demanded I sleep with him to repay the debt, or else he would prevent my son from graduating. I refused to believe my son would borrow money from him. As we argued, he showed me the IOU, leaving me speechless and collapsing to the ground. Boss Zhen sneered and said, “If you want to protect your son, it depends on whether you’re willing to cooperate.”  
[Clue: A photocopy of Bai Zhuangyuan’s IOU for 200,000 yuan from Boss Zhen (due October 7).]  

After Boss Zhen left, I immediately called my son’s school to confront him about the loan. My son said he would explain everything when he returned for National Day, as it was too complicated to discuss over the phone.  
[Clue: Call records between me and my son.]  

On October 1, 1998, my son finally came home. The moment I saw him, I burst into tears. He then confessed the real reason for borrowing the money—he wanted to start a business and pursue his dreams. Though I was furious, feeling he was just like Lao Bai with his unrealistic ambitions, I also saw the confidence, determination, and courage in his words. After much thought, I realized I shouldn’t blame him; he was chasing his dreams. So, I decided to mortgage the video store and our house to Boss Zhen to repay the debt.  

On the day of the incident (October 5, 1998), it drizzled all day.  
Around 18:40, I took the mortgage contracts for the store and house to negotiate with Boss Zhen. To my shock, he claimed they weren’t worth 200,000 yuan and insisted I sleep with him. Otherwise, he said, the debt would keep growing, and we’d never repay it. Enraged by his shameless demands, I argued back fiercely. As our quarrel escalated, Boss Zhen tried to assault me. I fought back desperately and barely managed to escape the grocery store.  
[Clue: Strangulation marks on my neck from resisting Boss Zhen’s assault.]  

At 19:00, I ran home crying and saw my son at the doorstep. I hugged him tightly. He kept asking what had happened. I hesitated, but overwhelmed with emotion, I eventually told him about Boss Zhen’s vile conditions and the assault. Furious, my son stormed out. At that moment, I had no strength left to chase after him and sat on the ground, weeping silently...  
By 20:00, after a long silence, an idea formed in my mind—I would steal back my son’s IOU.

In desperation, Bai Zhuangyuan borrowed 50,000 yuan from Boss Zhen and pooled together another 50,000 yuan with his friends to make up the 100,000 yuan. On September 20, 1998, Bai Zhuangyuan received a call from his mother and learned that Boss Zhen had told her about the loan. To avoid worrying her, Bai Zhuangyuan told his mother he would explain everything when he returned home for the National Day holiday.  

On October 5, 1998 (the day of the incident), Bai Zhuangyuan discovered that ever since he borrowed the money, Boss Zhen had been harassing his mother. He also found out that Boss Zhen had altered the IOU by adding a clause: "One month later, Bai Zhuangyuan must repay 200,000 yuan, including principal and interest. If repayment is delayed, a daily interest rate of 10% will apply."  

Furious, Bai Zhuangyuan went to the arcade to vent his anger by playing games. The more he thought about it, the angrier he became, and he decided to kill Boss Zhen.  

At 19:00, Bai Zhuangyuan planned to go to the video store to meet his mother but learned that Boss Zhen had been harassing her since the loan was taken, even proposing that she marry him to settle the debt.  

At 19:10, Bai Zhuangyuan rushed to Boss Zhen’s grocery store intending to beat him up but ended up being beaten instead. During the altercation, Bai Zhuangyuan discovered the altered IOU. Boss Zhen threatened him, demanding repayment the next day, and kicked him out of the store.  

At 19:30, Bai Zhuangyuan returned home and searched online for "how to repay debt quickly." He came across a post about "T7 venting."  

At 19:45, Bai Zhuangyuan went to the arcade and started playing games. As his anger grew, he resolved to kill Boss Zhen.  

At 21:10, Sa Bawang left the arcade in a hurry for an urgent matter. After Sa Bawang left, Bai Zhuangyuan searched the arcade for a "weapon." He took a large ice block from the freezer (used for making shaved ice), wrapped it in a cloth, grabbed an umbrella, and left through the arcade’s back door, heading toward the grocery store. As a result, he did not run into Sa Bawang, who was on his way back home.  

At 21:20, Bai Zhuangyuan arrived at the grocery store and found Boss Zhen drunk and asleep at the counter. He used the ice block to kill Boss Zhen. During the process, the ice melted, leaving water stains on Bai Zhuangyuan’s sleeve and on the floor near Boss Zhen’s feet. After confirming Boss Zhen was dead, Bai Zhuangyuan hurriedly left the store and discarded the ice and cloth in nearby bushes. The ice melted, leaving no trace.  

At 21:30, Bai Zhuangyuan returned to the arcade. He continued playing games while waiting for Boss Zhen’s body to be discovered.  

At 21:45, Gui Shaonü came to the arcade but left after a few minutes.  

At 21:55, Sa Bawang returned to the arcade, and Bai Zhuangyuan invited him to play games together.  

At 22:30, Bai Zhuangyuan heard the news that Boss Zhen had been killed.
